query: Which material can be used for enhance glass-forming ability, and why?

generation.hypothesis: The addition of certain elements, such as Al, Cr, and Si, to refractory high-entropy alloys can enhance their glass-forming ability by forming a dense oxidation film on the surface of the alloy in a high-temperature environment.
generation.intervention: Addition of Al, Cr, and Si elements
generation.mechanism: Formation of a dense oxidation film on the surface of the alloy
generation.uncertainty: The exact mechanism of how the addition of Al, Cr, and Si elements enhances the glass-forming ability of refractory high-entropy alloys is not fully understood and requires further research.

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of Al, Cr, and Si elements does not result in a significant increase in oxidation film thickness and glass-forming ability, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) first appeared in public view in 2010 [ [1] ]. Thereafter, they aroused great concern from researchers at home and abroad. Research has proved that RHEAs have excellent mechanical properties at high temperatures, even surpassing the widely used nickel-based alloy [ [2] , [3] , [4] , [5] , [6] ]. RHEAs, with excellent mechanical properties at elevated temperatures, are considered promising high-temperature application materials, which are suitable for complex working conditions such as atomic energy, aerospace, the military industry, advanced nuclear reactors, etc. Previous studies focused on mechanical properties at high- and room-temperatures, but with little research and analysis on high-temperature oxidation resistance [ [7] , [8] , [9] ]. The research shows that adding the proper amount of Al, Cr, and Si elements into the refractory high-entropy alloy can form a dense oxidation film on the surface of the alloy in a high-temperature environment, thus improving the high-temperature oxidation resistance [ [10] , [11] , [12] , [13] ].
